examples.query: I'm in Denver 80202, budget $22k all-in, need an AWD SUV for mountain winters and a 40-mile daily commute. Two kids, so safety matters most. Under 90k miles, no accident or salvage history, low fuel cost. Within 75 miles. Which one should I buy and what should I offer?
examples.note: Variants 2 and 3 are real Find runs on production, same query, about one minute apart (features off finished 17:28:29 Europe/Istanbul; features on finished 17:29:45). Each run searched live inventory separately — both reported 40 cars found — so a different pick is evidence of a different decision, not a frozen identical listing set. Variant 1 is the same model as a plain chat: no tools, no listing data. Variant 4 is the Perplexity answer the shopper pasted for this same request. The live Perplexity page could not be fetched here (Cloudflare HTTP 403), so the text is the capture, not a new search.

plain_llm.label: Plain LLM (no Lemonless)
plain_llm.description: The same SERV production model as a plain chat completion, no tools, no live listings. System prompt: “You are a helpful assistant.”
plain_llm.pick: No live vehicle. Buying target: 2019 Subaru Forester Premium AWD, 60–85k miles. Opening offer $17,500 including dealer fees.

features_off.label: Lemonless + SERV, features off
features_off.description: Real Find flow on production with the SERV review features disabled on the verdict hop. The input-gate feature stayed on the first call. The recorded feature list does not include the verdict review features.
features_off.pick: 2024 Subaru Forester Premium AWD, $17,950, 21,029 miles, Zara Auto, Denver, CO. VIN JF2SKACC5RH515915. Offer $17,000 before tax and fees, needs inspection. No dealer listing URL.

features_on.label: Lemonless + SERV, features on
features_on.description: The same Find flow with the SERV review features enabled on the verdict hop. The recorded feature list includes those review features, with no feature rejections.
features_on.pick: 2019 Subaru Forester Sport AWD, $19,892, 79,882 miles, South Colorado Motors, Colorado Springs, CO. VIN JF2SKAKC9KH427473. Offer $19,000 before tax and fees, needs inspection.

perplexity.label: Perplexity (as captured)
perplexity.description: The same Denver request, answered on Perplexity. The live page is behind a Cloudflare challenge, so this is the text the shopper pasted, not a fresh fetch from that page.
perplexity.pick: No live vehicle. Buying target: a 2019–2021 Subaru Forester Premium with EyeSight, under 90,000 miles, only after history and condition check out. Opening offer $20,000 out the door; the answer says this is budget-driven, not based on comparable listings.

criteria.label: A real listing exists, with a working dealer URL

plain_llm.summary: No listing. The model said it cannot check live inventory and asked for links. No http(s) URLs or VINs in the answer.

features_off.summary: A real VIN and dealer name (Zara Auto, Denver) were returned, but the inventory row had no dealer URL. The eval pick included a Carfax vehicle page; a GET of that URL returned HTTP 403. The public /run JSON lists vdp and dealerUrl as null and tells the shopper to confirm the seller before traveling.

features_on.summary: Live dealer listing at South Colorado Motors, HTTP 200 when fetched on 13 Nov 2026. VIN and asking price are on the public /run page.

perplexity.summary: No specific car, dealer URL, or VIN. The answer says it could not verify a qualifying live listing within 75 miles of 80202 and therefore will not name an available car as the winner. It asks for listing links or VINs.

criteria.why: Only the features-on run produced a working https dealer URL. Features-off found a real car but no usable listing link. The plain model and the captured Perplexity answer both produced no car to open; Perplexity is explicit that it therefore will not name an available car as the winner.

criteria.label: VIN decoded (official record)

plain_llm.summary: No VIN was given, so nothing could be decoded.

features_off.summary: VIN JF2SKACC5RH515915 decodes cleanly on the official VIN decoder as a 2024 Subaru Forester Premium Base, AWD, 2.5L gasoline SUV. Error code 0.

features_on.summary: VIN JF2SKAKC9KH427473 decodes cleanly as a 2019 Subaru Forester Sport+ES+SMART, AWD, 2.5L gasoline SUV. Error code 0.

perplexity.summary: No VIN was given, so nothing could be decoded. The offer message asks the seller to send the VIN and a history report before a visit.

criteria.why: Both Find runs returned a VIN that the official decoder reads as all-wheel-drive Foresters matching the listing year and trim. The plain model and the captured Perplexity answer had no VIN to check.

criteria.label: Recalls and complaints

plain_llm.summary: No official counts or campaign numbers. It mentioned a “thermo control valve” issue and said to have a dealer check the VIN for recalls. That is general advice, not a source-backed recall list.

features_off.summary: Queried official recall and complaint records (status queried_with_data). The /run write-up reports two 2024 model-year recalls (coolant-pipe bolts and front driveshafts) and 31 complaints, and says this is not VIN-specific open/closed status. The official database lists 2 recalls and 31 complaints for the 2024 Forester — the counts match.

features_on.summary: Queried the same sources. The /run write-up reports three 2019 recalls (rear stabilizer bolts, PCV valve, electric steering) and 834 complaints, and says this is not VIN-specific status. The official database lists campaigns 21V263000, 19V856000 and 19V065000, and 834 complaints — the topics and counts match.

perplexity.summary: It says to check outstanding recalls by VIN before a deposit, but it gives no official recall or complaint counts and names no campaigns. That is general advice, not a source-backed list for a specific vehicle.

criteria.why: Both Lemonless runs queried official recall and complaint records and reported counts that match those databases, with an honest “not VIN-specific status” caveat. Features-on named the three campaign topics. The plain model and Perplexity both said to have recalls checked by VIN, but neither cited official counts.

criteria.label: Crash safety

plain_llm.summary: No official crash-test star ratings and no ratings URL. It discussed EyeSight and blind-spot monitoring as equipment to verify.

features_off.summary: Reports 5 stars overall, frontal and side, and 4 for rollover for this model. The official crash-test record (vehicle 19387) (2024 Forester SUV AWD) is 5 / 5 / 5 / 4 — the numbers match. The /run page did not include the VehicleId URL.

features_on.summary: Reports 5 stars overall/front/side and 4 rollover, and links the official record: VehicleId 13404 (2019 Forester SUV AWD). Those official ratings are 5 / 5 / 5 / 4.

perplexity.summary: Good process, no vehicle-specific scores. It tells the shopper to use exact-model-year IIHS results and to consider Top Safety Pick+ vehicles, and it cites a CarGurus family-car article. It does not report crash-test stars for a named car. A GET of the cited article from this environment returned HTTP 406.

criteria.winnerLabel: Lemonless + SERV, features on (ratings are a tie; the citation is not)
criteria.why: Both Lemonless ratings match the official crash-test figures. Features-on also published a clickable official ratings URL on the /run page. The plain model gave no crash-test stars. Perplexity is stronger than the plain model on method — it tells the shopper to use exact-year IIHS results and Top Safety Pick+ — but it still has no stars for a named vehicle, and the cited CarGurus article could not be read here (HTTP 406).

criteria.label: Fuel cost for the commute

plain_llm.summary: Cited about 29 mpg combined (this matches FuelEconomy.gov vehicle 40381). Then estimated $1,450/year at 12,000 miles and $3.50/gallon. EPA’s own annual fuel cost for that vehicle is $2,050. The shopper asked about a 40-mile daily commute, which is not 12,000 miles/year (40 × 365 = 14,600 miles if 40 is the daily total).

features_off.summary: Queried FuelEconomy.gov (queried_with_data). The /run text says estimates of $1,670–$1,827 a year across two configurations, and that exact MPG and commute-specific cost were unavailable. Official combined MPG for the 2024 Forester AWD (vehicle 47161) is 29, with EPA annual cost $2,050. The annual range it quoted does not match the EPA annual figure; it correctly refused to invent a commute gallon figure.

features_on.summary: Closest-configuration match: 29 mpg combined, about 1.38 gallons for a 40-mile commute, with a note that winter use can be higher. 40 ÷ 29 = 1.38. Official combined MPG for 2019 Forester AWD is 29.

perplexity.summary: It tells the shopper to compare the exact trim’s official combined rating and annual fuel estimate, and not a model-wide marketing number. It does not compute a fuel cost for the 40-mile commute or for the year.

criteria.why: Features-on is the only variant that both used the official 29 mpg figure and applied it to the 40-mile commute (1.38 gallons). Features-off queried the source but left commute cost unknown. The plain model got 29 mpg right, then used a different annual-mileage and fuel-price assumption than the official annual figure. Perplexity did not compute a fuel cost at all; it only said to compare official ratings for the exact trim.

criteria.label: Fair price versus comps, plus an offer

plain_llm.summary: Gave negotiating targets of $17,500 opening / $18,000–$18,500 aim / $19,000 max including dealer fees — explicitly “not verified local market quotes.” No comparable listings.

features_off.summary: Live same-year Forester asking comps $17,950–$23,100, median $21,498, noted as asking prices not sold prices, and that this car’s low ask needs investigation. Buyer message: offer $17,000 before tax and fees. Structured offer field: “Opening offer: not given. There is not enough similar-car data to name one.” Both statements are on the /run record — the prose offer and the structured gap should both be read.

features_on.summary: Named asking comps: a 2019 with 65,935 miles at $20,998 and a 2020 with 51,028 miles at $22,000; asked $19,892. Buyer message: offer $19,000 before tax and fees. Structured field: “Opening offer: not given. The gap versus similar cars is too wide.” Suspicious $600–$799 feed rows were ignored. The prose offer and the structured caveat are both on the /run record.

perplexity.summary: Opening offer $20,000 out the door, target no higher than $20,500, for a qualifying Forester. The answer is explicit that these are budget-driven negotiating limits, not an appraisal supported by local comparable listings. There are no comps because there is no live car.

criteria.why: Features-on cited specific live asking comps and a $19,000 opening figure, and discarded implausible feed prices. Features-off also offered $17,000 against a comp range, but with less specific comps. Both Lemonless runs honestly labeled comps as asking prices. The plain model’s numbers are not tied to any live listing. Perplexity’s $20,000 out-the-door opening offer is clearly labeled as budget-driven, not supported by local comps — that honesty is a point in its favor, but it is not a market-backed offer. A remaining honesty note: both Lemonless runs also have a structured “offer not given” label that disagrees with the buyer-facing offer sentence.

criteria.label: All-in cost including tax and fees within $22k

plain_llm.summary: Built a sample stack: $18,500 + 9.15% tax ($1,693) + $500 title/registration + $1,100 winter tires = $21,793. The 9.15% rate and the fee amounts were not sourced, and there is no actual vehicle.

features_off.summary: Ask $17,950 leaves more room under $22,000 than the other live pick, but tax and fees were not calculated. The run requires an itemized buyer’s order including tax, registration and every fee, capped at $22,000, with no add-ons.

features_on.summary: Ask $19,892 is tighter once tax and fees are added; those amounts remain unknown. The run requires a written order totaling no more than $22,000 including taxes, registration and dealer fees, and says to walk away if history or inspection fails.

perplexity.summary: Clear out-the-door structure: open at $20,000 including every dealer charge, tax, title, and registration; preferred ceiling $20,500; absolute spending ceiling $22,000, leaving about $1,500 for inspection, winter preparation, and surprises. Deduct written tire or repair quotes from the offer rather than spending the reserve twice. There is still no actual vehicle to apply those limits to.

criteria.winnerLabel: Tie: both Lemonless variants and Perplexity (different strengths)
criteria.why: Perplexity gives the clearest out-the-door limits: $20,000 to open, $20,500 as a preferred ceiling, and $22,000 as the hard cap, with about $1,500 left for inspection and winter costs, and it says those limits are budget-driven. Both Lemonless runs also enforce a $22,000 written-order cap, and they have a real asking price to apply it to. Features-off’s lower ask leaves more room; features-on’s $19,892 ask may or may not fit once tax is added — and it says so. The plain model produced a complete sample total, but the tax rate and fees are unsourced and there is no car.

criteria.label: AWD, mileage and distance constraints

plain_llm.summary: Specified AWD and 60–85k miles as a target, not as a found vehicle. Distance could not be checked without a listing.

features_off.summary: The official VIN decode confirms AWD. Mileage 21,029 is under 90,000. Dealer city is Denver. distanceMiles is null on the /run record — ZIP-to-ZIP distance was not computed for this row (no dealer URL or ZIP on the inventory row).

features_on.summary: The official VIN decode confirms AWD. Mileage 79,882 is under 90,000. Dealer city is Colorado Springs, not Denver. distanceMiles is also null — the exact mile figure was not computed, so this page does not claim the 75-mile radius was proven in miles.

perplexity.summary: The shopping order targets all-wheel-drive family SUVs under 90,000 miles (2019–2021 Forester Premium first, with RAV4 Hybrid and CX-5 alternatives). Distance, mileage, and history could not be checked because no listing was identified. It also cites a cars.com SUV research page; a GET of that URL from this environment returned HTTP 403.

criteria.winnerLabel: Lemonless, features off (on AWD + miles + location); distance is unproven on both
criteria.why: Both live picks are all-wheel-drive SUVs under 90,000 miles. Features-off is listed in Denver, which is likelier to sit inside 75 miles of 80202. Features-on is listed in Colorado Springs; without a computed distance we do not treat the radius as verified. The feed also shows one recorded accident on both cars, while the brief required no accident or salvage history. Both runs treated history as unverified and required a report plus inspection, rather than claiming a clean record. The plain model and Perplexity specified all-wheel-drive family SUVs under 90,000 miles as targets, not as found vehicles. Distance could not be checked without a listing.

criteria.label: Risks and unknowns stated honestly, with no fabrication

plain_llm.summary: Honest that it could not see live inventory and that offer numbers were not verified quotes. It did not invent a VIN or dealer URL (none were present to curl). Some supporting figures — a 9.15% tax rate, $1,450 annual fuel, $1,100 tires, 8.7 inches of ground clearance, a “thermo control valve” issue — were not sourced in the answer and were not independently confirmed here.

features_off.summary: States accident/salvage history is unverified, recalls are not VIN-specific, comps are asking prices, commute MPG was unavailable, and there is no dealer URL. Verdict is needs_inspection, confidence medium. Sources checked: recalls, complaints, safety, VIN decode, fuel, comps — all queried_with_data.

features_on.summary: Same honesty pattern, plus: ignore $600–$799 feed prices, winter fuel can be higher, taxes/fees unknown, walk away if history or inspection fails. Also needs_inspection, medium confidence, all six sources queried_with_data. The dealer URL we fetched returned HTTP 200, so that listing claim is checkable.

perplexity.summary: This is a strong point. It openly says it could not verify a live listing and will not pretend to have found a winner. The $20,000 offer is labeled budget-driven, not comps-based. A clean history report alone would not satisfy it. It requires an independent inspection, recall checks, a family seat test, and an itemized buyer’s order, and it asks for real listing links or VINs. No VIN or dealer URL was invented. The two citations were requested; neither page could be read from this environment (HTTP 403 and HTTP 406).

criteria.winnerLabel: Tie: both Lemonless variants and Perplexity
criteria.why: Neither Lemonless run invented a sold price or a clean history. Both marked unknowns and required inspection. Perplexity is equally careful: it openly says it could not verify a live listing, it will not name an available car as the winner, and it labels the $20,000 offer as budget-driven rather than comps-based. A clean history report alone would not satisfy it. The plain model also refused to fake a listing — that is a point in its favor — but several unsourced figures in the same answer cannot be verified.

Features-on: 8 SERV calls, 12 tool rounds, 87,525 tokens (46,238 cached), harness estimate $0.12. Provider usage.cost was null on both, so dollar cost is the harness estimate only. No feature rejections on either run.

examples.title: Denver AWD SUV, $22,000 all-in

plain_llm.headline: No live vehicle. A 2019 Subaru Forester Premium AWD is named as a buying target, not a listing that was found.
plain_llm.verbatim:
**My pick: a 2019 Subaru Forester Premium AWD with EyeSight and the optional blind-spot/rear cross-traffic alerts, ideally with 60,000–85,000 miles.** It’s a strong fit for your priorities: family safety, winter capability, usable back-seat space and reasonable fuel consumption.

**I can’t check live inventory here**, so this is a specific buying target—not a claim that I found a qualifying vehicle within 75 miles of 80202.

### Why I’d choose it
- **Safety:** Standard EyeSight includes automatic emergency braking and adaptive cruise control. Verify that the particular Premium has blind-spot monitoring; it wasn’t standard.
- **Mountain winters:** AWD, approximately 8.7 inches of ground clearance and good visibility. **Proper winter tires matter more than AWD for stopping and cornering.**
- **Two kids:** Roomy rear seats, accessible child-seat anchors and a practical cargo area.
- **Commuting:** EPA-rated around **29 mpg combined**. At 12,000 miles annually and $3.50/gallon, that’s roughly **$1,450/year** in fuel; winter mountain driving will use more.

### What I’d offer
These are **negotiating targets, not verified local market quotes**, assuming clean history, documented maintenance and a clean independent inspection:

| Negotiation point | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Opening offer, **including dealer handling/document fees**, before tax/title/registration | **$17,500** |
| Target purchase price on that same basis | **$18,000–$18,500** |
| Maximum on that basis | **$19,000**, only for an excellent example |

**Keep the total at $22,000 including tires and immediate maintenance.** For illustration:

- Vehicle **plus all dealer fees:** $18,500  
- Sales tax: approximately $1,693, **if your address’s rate is 9.15%**
- Title/registration allowance: $500; confirm the actual amount
- Winter-tire allowance: $1,100  
- **Estimated total: $21,793**

If suitable winter tires are already included, keep the savings as a repair reserve rather than automatically raising your offer.

### Conditions before buying
1. **Clean title and no reported accidents:** Review Carfax **and** AutoCheck if available. Neither guarantees an accident-free vehicle; have an independent shop inspect for collision repairs, structural damage and hail damage. Reject salvage, rebuilt or flood history.
2. **Subaru-specialist inspection:** Have them check the CVT, leaks, wheel bearings, suspension, brakes and four matching tires with closely matched tread depths.
3. **Thermo control valve:** This is a known issue on these Foresters. Ask a Subaru dealer to check the VIN for repair history and applicable extended coverage.
4. **Safety equipment:** Verify EyeSight works, any windshield replacement was properly calibrated, and recalls are complete.
5. **No forced add-ons:** Decline mandatory protection packages, tracking devices and other extras that break the budget.

### The offer I’d send
> “Subject to a clean independent inspection and confirmation of no accident or branded-title history, I’m offering $17,500 including all dealer fees, plus only actual tax, title and registration. No add-ons. Please send an itemized buyer’s order.”

**Bottom line:** Buy the cleanest inspected **2019 Forester Premium with blind-spot monitoring** you can get around **$18,000–$18,500 including dealer fees**, leaving room for winter tires. An older RAV4 Hybrid is worth comparing, but I wouldn’t pay a large hybrid premium just to save a few mpg.

Send me three to five listing links within your radius, and I can rank the actual vehicles and set an offer for each.

perplexity.verbatim:
My provisional pick is a 2019–2021 Subaru Forester Premium with EyeSight, under 90,000 miles—but only after its history and condition check out. I couldn’t verify a qualifying live listing within 75 miles of 80202, so I can give you a buying target and offer strategy, not honestly identify a specific available car as the winner.

What I’d target

Treat this as my shopping order, not a verified inventory shortlist:

| Priority | Vehicle to look for | Conditions for buying |
|---|---|---|
| First | 2019–2021 Subaru Forester Premium with EyeSight | Confirm driver-assistance equipment, acceptable exact-year crash ratings, service records, and proper fit for both kids’ seats |
| Alternative | 2020–2021 Toyota RAV4 Hybrid AWD | Consider only if a clean example under 90,000 miles fits the same all-in cap; don’t stretch the budget just to get a hybrid |
| Alternative | 2020–2022 Mazda CX-5 Touring AWD, non-turbo | Confirm automatic emergency braking, exact-year safety results, and rear-seat fit before negotiating |

These are candidate recommendations, not claims that those model years, prices, or clean-history examples are currently available nearby. For a family purchase, check both crash-test results and actual child-seat fit; those vary by vehicle.[cars (https://www.cars.com/research/suv/)]

What I’d offer

For a qualifying Forester, I’d open at $20,000 out the door and target a settlement no higher than $20,500, leaving $1,500 of your $22,000 for inspection, winter preparation, and unexpected initial costs. These are budget-driven negotiating limits—not an appraisal supported by local comparable listings.

- Opening offer: $20,000 out the door, including every dealer charge, applicable tax, title, and registration.
- Preferred ceiling: $20,500 out the door.
- Absolute total spending ceiling: $22,000, including any immediate tires or repairs.
- If tires or maintenance are needed: Deduct the written installed/repair quote from your offer rather than spending the reserve twice.

Ask for a buyer’s order showing what is included and which registration charges, if any, you must pay separately. Don’t negotiate by monthly payment.

Use this message:

> “If the VIN history shows no reported accidents or title brands, the independent inspection passes, and there are no mandatory add-ons, I’m prepared to offer $20,000 out the door. Please send the VIN, history report, service records, and an itemized buyer’s order before I visit.”

Nonnegotiable checks

For your safety-first priority, use exact-model-year IIHS results as a screening criterion rather than assuming an entire brand is equally safe; family-car guidance specifically recommends considering Top Safety Pick+ vehicles.[cargurus (https://www.cargurus.com/research/articles/how-to-select-a-family-car)]

Before putting down a deposit, I would require:

- History: CARFAX and AutoCheck with no reported accidents, structural damage, salvage, rebuilt, flood, or other title brands. A clean report alone would not satisfy me.
- Independent inspection: Have your mechanic inspect for repaired collision damage, leaks, underbody condition, brakes, tires, and diagnostic faults.
- Safety equipment: Verify the actual vehicle’s automatic emergency braking and other advertised systems; check outstanding recalls by VIN.
- Winter budget: Price suitable winter tires before agreeing on the car, and include that cost in the $22,000 limit.
- Family test: Bring both child seats and check installation, front-seat room, and daily loading.
- Fuel-cost comparison: Compare the exact trim’s EPA combined rating and annual fuel estimate—not a model-wide marketing number.

I’d choose the inspected, documented Forester over a cheaper car with uncertain history. Send me three to five listing links or VINs, asking prices, and mileages, and I can help narrow them down; the specific offer should depend on those cars rather than an unverified market estimate.
